characters.name: Buck
characters.notes: St. Bernard-Scotch shepherd mix; protagonist whose arc is decivilization and answering the wild call

characters.name: Judge Miller
characters.notes: Buck's original owner in Santa Clara Valley

characters.name: Manuel
characters.notes: Gardener's helper who kidnaps Buck to fund gambling

characters.name: man in the red sweater
characters.notes: Dog-breaker in Seattle who teaches Buck the law of the club

characters.name: Perrault
characters.notes: French-Canadian government courier; buys Buck

characters.name: Francois
characters.notes: French-Canadian half-breed dog-driver; fair and skilled

characters.name: Spitz
characters.notes: Treacherous white lead dog; Buck's rival to the death

characters.name: Curly
characters.notes: Good-natured Newfoundland; killed by huskies on Dyea beach

characters.name: Dave
characters.notes: Experienced wheeler; dies in harness from internal injury

characters.name: Sol-leks
characters.notes: One-eyed husky; blind-side sensitive

characters.name: Billee
characters.notes: Good-natured husky brother of Joe

characters.name: Joe
characters.notes: Sour, malignant husky brother of Billee

characters.name: Pike
characters.notes: Clever malingerer and thief on the team

characters.name: Dub
characters.notes: Awkward blunderer; later shot by Hal

characters.name: Hal
characters.notes: Callow young man from the States; cruel incompetent owner

characters.name: Charles
characters.notes: Middle-aged weak-eyed man; Mercedes's husband

characters.name: Mercedes
characters.notes: Charles's wife and Hal's sister; soft, weeping, rides the sled

characters.name: John Thornton
characters.notes: Ideal master who rescues and loves Buck; withheld as savior until White River

characters.name: Skeet
characters.notes: Irish setter; nurses Buck's wounds

characters.name: Nig
characters.notes: Huge friendly black dog half bloodhound half deerhound

characters.name: Hans
characters.notes: Thornton's partner

characters.name: Pete
characters.notes: Thornton's partner

characters.name: Matthewson
characters.notes: Bonanza King who bets against Buck

characters.name: Yeehats
characters.notes: Indigenous hunters who massacre Thornton's camp

characters.name: wild brother
characters.notes: Lean wolf Buck befriends and later runs with

characters.name: hairy man
characters.notes: Ancestral vision figure Buck sees by the fire

locations_mentioned: Judge Miller's place, Santa Clara Valley
timeline: Fall 1897: Buck at Judge Miller's; Klondike strike begins
Night of Manuel's treachery; kidnapping to San Francisco then Seattle
Broken by man in red sweater; sold to Perrault
Voyage north on Narwhal; first snow at Dyea
First trail season: Curly killed; harness work; rivalry with Spitz builds
Starving husky attack at Lake Le Barge; hard ice travel
Buck kills Spitz; becomes lead dog; record run to Skaguay
Mail run back to Dawson; Dave dies in traces
Sold to Hal/Charles/Mercedes; disastrous overloaded trip
Spring: dogs collapse at White River; Thornton rescues Buck
Summer convalescence and love; river rescue; Burton fight
Winter Dawson: thousand-pound pull bet won
Journey east seeking Lost Cabin; find rich placer instead
Months of wandering; call intensifies; meets wild brother
Kills great bull moose; returns to find camp destroyed by Yeehats
Avenges Thornton; joins wolf pack; becomes Ghost Dog of legend

Do not reveal Buck will kill Spitz until the rabbit-chase fight in B14; keep rivalry as simmering threat
Do not show or name the Yeehats or camp massacre before B26; keep eastern journey as gold-seeking idyll until return
Do not confirm Buck fully answers the call and joins the pack until B27 after Thornton's death is established
Withhold the Ghost Dog / brown-splash wolf-pack epilogue until final beat B28
The hairy-man ancestral visions may appear from B17 onward but never be explained as literal flashback until Buck's full wild transformation

essential_beats.summary: Establish Buck as pampered king of Judge Miller's sun-kissed Santa Clara estate; introduce gold-rush demand for strong dogs.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Buck rules the great demesne, hunts and swims with the family, weighs 140 pounds, lives as sated aristocrat while men rush north for yellow metal.

essential_beats.summary: Manuel, needing lottery money, steals Buck at night and sells him at College Park station.
essential_beats.source_evidence: On the night Judge is at a meeting, Manuel ropes Buck, delivers him to a stranger for money; Buck is choked and thrown into a baggage car.

essential_beats.summary: Brutal journey south then north: crate, thirst, teasing expressmen; arrives Seattle half-mad with rage.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Buck rides two days without food or water, attacks handlers, is filed out of collar and crated; express messengers torment him until Seattle.

essential_beats.summary: Man in red sweater clubs Buck into submission; Buck learns a man with a club is lawgiver.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Buck charges repeatedly; club smashes him senseless; afterward he accepts water and meat but never forgets the lesson of primitive law.

essential_beats.summary: Perrault buys Buck and Curly; voyage on Narwhal; first snow and introduction to Francois, Spitz, Dave.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Sold for three hundred; meets treacherous Spitz and morose Dave; ship grows colder; Buck tastes snow and is ashamed.

essential_beats.summary: Dyea beach nightmare: Curly is torn apart by huskies the moment she goes down; Buck vows never to go down.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Friendly Curly is ripped open then buried under thirty huskies; Francois axes them off too late; Spitz laughs; Buck learns no fair play.

essential_beats.summary: Buck is harnessed for the first time; learns commands under Francois, Dave and Spitz; new huskies Billee, Joe, Sol-leks join.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Dignity hurt but he pulls firewood; stops at 'ho', goes at 'mush'; Spitz disciplines newcomers; Sol-leks slashes Buck for blind-side approach.

essential_beats.summary: First night: Buck learns to dig a snow nest after being driven from the tent; wakes buried and panics like a wild thing.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Driven out with curses; finds Billee under snow; digs own hole and sleeps; morning fear of trap then recognition of camp.

essential_beats.summary: Hard trail to Lake Bennett and beyond; Buck steals food, loses moral nature, instincts awaken; howls at stars.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Ration too small; copies Pike's theft; becomes callous, keen-sensed; ancestral fight tricks and wolf howl return; decivilization complete.

essential_beats.summary: Dominant beast grows in Buck; Spitz bullies; nest fight interrupted by starving husky horde that guts the camp.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Buck avoids open war until Spitz steals nest; they tangle; then scores of famished huskies raid grub and wound the team.

essential_beats.summary: Thirty Mile River hell; Buck's feet freeze; Dolly goes mad and is axed; Spitz savages exhausted Buck; open war declared.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Six days of thin ice and drownings; Francois makes moccasins; mad Dolly chases Buck; Spitz tears him; Francois predicts Buck will kill Spitz.

essential_beats.summary: Buck systematically undermines Spitz's authority; team solidarity collapses; continual bickering on the Dawson run.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Buck shields shirkers; Pike steals under Buck's protection; Francois's whip cannot restore order; Spitz no longer feared.

essential_beats.summary: Snowshoe-rabbit chase under aurora; sixty dogs in full cry; Spitz cuts off rabbit; Buck and Spitz fight to the death.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Ecstasy of the kill-run; Spitz takes rabbit; circle of wolves waits; Buck breaks both forelegs then finishes Spitz; stands dominant primordial beast.

essential_beats.summary: Next morning Buck demands lead position; refuses Sol-leks; after hour-long standoff Francois yields; Buck proves superb leader.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Buck displaces Sol-leks twice; dodges clubs; men finally throw club down; Buck swings into lead and enforces discipline instantly.

essential_beats.summary: Record fourteen-day run to Skaguay; team leaps as one; Francois weeps farewell; Scotch half-breed takes mail train.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Forty-mile days; Thirty Mile covered in one; Skaguay worship; official orders separate Buck from Perrault and Francois forever.

essential_beats.summary: Heavy mail toil; Buck masters camp dogs; fire-side visions of hairy ancestral man; Dave sickens and dies in harness.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Eighteen hundred miles tell; Dave cries in traces, bites free to reclaim place, is shot behind timber; Buck knows.

essential_beats.summary: Salt Water Mail arrives Skaguay wrecked; sold cheap to Hal, Charles and Mercedes; slipshod overloaded outfit.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Dogs down to skeletons; three days rest then bought for a song; tent half-pitched, dishes unwashed, woman fluttering.

essential_beats.summary: First start fails; top-heavy sled capsizes in street; citizens advise half load twice dogs; outsiders added; food math doomed.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Whip and tears; runners frozen; load spills; six Outside dogs bought; fourteen dogs cannot be fed by one sled.

essential_beats.summary: Incompetent trail: late starts, overfeeding then starvation; Dub shot; Outside dogs die; family quarrels; Mercedes rides.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Never make computed distance; horse-hide substitute; Billee axed; seven skeletons left; woman 120-pound last straw.

essential_beats.summary: Spring thaw; stagger into John Thornton's camp; Hal clubs Buck who refuses to rise; Thornton intervenes, cuts traces.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Rotten ice warning ignored; Buck beaten senseless; Thornton springs, knocks knife away, frees Buck; others drive onto ice and vanish.

essential_beats.summary: Thornton nurses Buck; Skeet and Nig befriend him; first true love; Buck will not let master out of sight.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Long spring rest; doctoring by setter; rough embraces and love-oaths; Buck adores at distance yet fears Thornton will vanish like others.

essential_beats.summary: Primitive strain remains; Buck steals from others but not Thornton; saves master from Burton's blow and from Forty-Mile rapids.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Roars and tears Burton's throat; later swims thrice into mill-race, three broken ribs, camps till healed; partners Hans and Pete arrive.

essential_beats.summary: Eldorado Saloon bet: Buck breaks out and pulls thousand-pound sled one hundred yards; wins sixteen hundred dollars.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Thornton bluffs then borrows stake; frozen runners; 'As you love me'; gee-haw-mush; crowd roars; Thornton refuses fortune for the dog.

essential_beats.summary: Partners outfit and head east for fabled Lost Cabin; wander seasons; find rich shallow placer instead and heap gold.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Seventy miles up Yukon then Stewart; Indian-fashion hunting; no cabin but butter-yellow gold; fifty-pound moose-hide sacks piled like firewood.

essential_beats.summary: Idle days; hairy-man visions intensify; forest call lures Buck; he runs with a timber wolf then returns to Thornton.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Restlessness; long-drawn howl; stalks lean wolf, plays, runs side by side across divide; remembers master and turns back; wolf howls mournfully.

essential_beats.summary: Blood-longing peaks; Buck pulls down great bull moose over four days; races home sensing calamity; finds Nig, Hans, Pete, Skeet dead; Thornton in pool.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Cuts bull from herd, wears it to death; fresh Yeehat trail; arrow-killed dogs; feathered Hans; lodge wrecked; scents last struggle into water.

essential_beats.summary: Buck goes berserk among Yeehats, kills chief and many; mourns Thornton; wolf pack arrives; after fight he howls and runs with them.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Hurricane of fury; throats ripped; Yeehats flee calling him Evil Spirit; night pack pours in; Buck breaks necks then sniffs noses with wild brother and old wolf; joins the song.

essential_beats.summary: Epilogue: Yeehats fear Ghost Dog that leads the pack; each summer a great wolf visits the gold-stream valley and howls once for the man.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Breed shows brown muzzle splashes; hunters found throat-slashed; valley never entered; lone wolf muses by rotted sacks then runs at head of pack singing the younger-world song.
